# @mintlify/cli

The Mintlify CLI. See [mintlify](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mintlify) for more documentation.

## Agent setup

Run `mint agent setup` to install [Mintlify skills](https://mintlify.com/docs/ai/skillmd) and configure the [Admin MCP](https://mintlify.com/docs/ai/mintlify-mcp) for Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. The command requires Node.js 22.20 or later and npm.

```sh
mint agent setup
mint agent setup --agent claude-code codex cursor
mint agent setup --agent codex --global
```

Setup defaults to the current project. Use `--global` for your user account. Pass `--agent` to configure specific agents directly. Otherwise, interactive setup lets you choose agents, with detected agents selected by default. Without a terminal, setup uses detected agents and requires `--agent` if none are detected.

Skills are installed with `npx --yes skills@1.7.4 add https://mintlify.com/docs`, using the selected agents and scope. Rerunning setup refreshes these downloaded skills and replaces local edits to them.

Admin MCP uses the server name `mintlify-admin` and URL `https://mcp.mintlify.com`. Setup preserves existing configuration and skips a matching server entry. A conflicting entry or invalid configuration stops setup before skills are installed. Codex configurations with an inline `mcp_servers` table need manual setup, as do global Claude Code configurations using `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

After configuration, complete OAuth sign-in in each agent to grant access to your Mintlify account and projects. In Claude Code, use `/mcp`; in Cursor, connect the server in MCP settings. For Codex project setup, the printed login command passes the server URL explicitly because some CLI versions do not read project configuration for `mcp login`. Global Codex setup uses `codex mcp login mintlify-admin`. Project configurations may require trusting the project and approving the server first. The command does not reuse `mint login` credentials or complete OAuth on your behalf.
